4.127.0
1:# Wrangler's experimental TypeScript configuration
3:Researched 2026-09-08; refreshed 2026-09-09 against Wrangler 4.130.0. This is an evaluation note, not an adopted configuration or migration plan.
5:Wrangler's “new config” is an experimental, executable TypeScript configuration model: `cloudflare.config.ts` describes the Worker, while optional `wrangler.config.ts` describes Wrangler's tooling. It shipped behind `--x-new-config` in Wrangler 4.100.0. The shared `@cloudflare/config` README still explicitly says it is unsuitable for stable external use and may change without notice. Cloudflare's current ordinary configuration documentation continues to recommend JSONC. Wrangler 4.130.0 materially improves composition: object-form configs can now be spread, and bindings can reference another config directly. This corrects the earlier composition restriction in this note. For cyspbot, these changes strengthen the case for a bounded prototype, while standalone type generation and existing config-path integration still require work. [4.130.0 config changes][config-changes] [Introduction][intro] · [Stability statement][stability] · [Current configuration docs][docs]
7:## Evidence boundary
11:- Latest verified npm release: Wrangler **4.130.0**, commit `570526276722ae57b250268a8af48fe0b1eaf774`, published September 8 at 17:09 UTC (September 9 in Sydney). Installed into a temporary directory and tested with Node **24.18.0**; the repository remains on 4.127.0. Its bundled shared configuration implementation corresponds to `@cloudflare/config` **0.11.0**. The command results below are refreshed 4.130.0 observations. [Release][release130] · [Config changes][config-changes]
14:## What changes
32:## Minimal example and modes
34:This basic shape remains suitable for the investigated 4.127.0, 4.129.1, and 4.130.0 APIs. The temporary fixture verified text/secret bindings and mode selection; this exact illustrative file is not a cyspbot deployment configuration.
68:An entrypoint can instead be imported with `import * as entrypoint from "./src/index.ts" with { type: "cf-worker" }`. The config loader substitutes a path reference and does not execute that Worker module; this also carries types into inference. Other configuration imports are executable Node code. The loader rejects Bun and requires Node support corresponding to 22.18.0 or higher. [Module loading][loading] · [Worker definition][definition]
70:There is no released `modes` override map in the inspected schema. A proposal for such a map was closed without merging; environment branching remains ordinary TypeScript. [Latest schema][latest-schema] · [Closed proposal][modes-proposal]
72:## New in 4.130.0: composition and Worker references
111:Object spread is shallow: spreading `base.env` explicitly preserves its bindings. Helpers and reusable values still belong in a separate module because config-file exports are validated as configuration exports. Both examples are illustrative; the local fixture used the same composition/reference pattern with a minimal Worker.
113:`bindings.worker({ worker: config })` and `bindings.durableObject({ worker: config, exportName: "Counter" })` now accept direct configuration references; string Worker names remain supported. Upstream type tests verify export-name checking and RPC/Durable Object inference. The loader resolves references with the same `ctx.mode` and caches their resolution by identity. A reference that is not itself exported supplies its resolved Worker name without fully validating/deploying that Worker. [Binding API][bindings] · [Type tests][reference-types] · [Reference loader][reference-loader]
117:## Command and tooling support
124:| `dev --x-new-config --local`                    | Reached ready locally and generated `worker-configuration.d.ts`, including `UnwrapConfig`, `InferEnv`, and `Cloudflare.Env`; warned about the missing declared secret. `dev.types.includeRuntime: false` was respected.       |
125:| `types --x-new-config`                          | Failed locally: `Unknown arguments: x-new-config, xNewConfig`. The new-config type-generation file is used by development, not this standalone command. Still fails in 4.130.0; its command source is unchanged from 4.129.1. |
131:The 4.130.0 command experiments are local observations, supported by the [build implementation][build], [loader][loader], [development type generator][dev-types], [standalone type command][latest-types], [initial release scope][intro], and first-party [Vite test][vite-new-config] / [new Vitest plugin fixture][vitest]. Running a command with `--help` is insufficient to test whether a hidden flag is accepted during execution.
133:Generated config-based types import the TypeScript config and infer its return type, rather than enumerating each selected deployment mode independently. Review the inferred union/optional types when branches expose different bindings. This follows the [generator][generator] and [inference implementation][inference]; the closed modes proposal also identifies this concern. [Proposal][modes-proposal]
135:## Migration limitations and ownership
139:**Binding parity is incomplete.** In the inspected 4.127.0 and 4.130.0 schemas, Workflow bindings remain excluded/commented out, Worker previews remain a TODO, and there is no top-level containers configuration. These are specific schema gaps, not evidence that all other legacy properties are supported. Inventory the fields actually needed before converting a real deployment. [4.127 schema][schema] · [4.130 schema][latest-schema]
141:**Secrets remain declarations.** `bindings.secret()` accepts no value and converts to `secrets.required`; it does not retrieve or inject a secret manager's values. The build-output model also serializes resolved configuration to disk. An August discussion proposes new ways to supply values, but those proposals are not an available API. Keep deployment secret injection in the existing deployment owner, and do not treat `bindings.text(process.env.SECRET)` as a secret binding. [Binding helper][bindings] · [Conversion][convert] · [Build-output discussion][secrets-discussion]
149:## Fit for cyspbot
151:The repository baseline remains `3f0cf76005c25372788acd14e29956e0d54b5a9b`. Its [package manifest](../../package.json) pins Wrangler 4.127.0 and `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` 0.22.0. The [Vitest configuration](../../vitest.config.ts) loads JSONC files through `wrangler.configPath`; Worker package scripts use explicit `--config` paths and standalone `wrangler types` generation/check commands. These are concrete integration points a migration would have to preserve or replace.
153:The separation could suit this repository's existing boundary: shared/public Worker definitions could express binding names and source settings, while the deployment repository supplies account IDs, production resource identities, routes, and secrets. That is a design opportunity, not implemented behavior; the existing ownership boundary remains authoritative. [Repository deployment documentation](../deployment.md)
155:Before adopting it, a disposable prototype should prove the existing generated-type checks, integration tests, config path selection, three-Worker local topology, and deployment-repository composition against pinned versions. 4.130.0 removes the object-composition obstacle and improves typed cross-Worker references. The observed standalone `types` failure, fixed config filename, different Vitest integration, and released schema churn still prevent a direct conversion of the existing workflow. A useful next experiment is to compose one public Worker config with deployment-owned overrides, then prove type-checking and test integration without duplicating the configuration. No application configuration was changed by this research.

Wrangler **4.131.1** resolves to **`00ae21fa83754462721a52bcd1ff9b4fbc12f898`**. Its release comparison against 4.130.0 contains 32 commits. [Release](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/releases/tag/wrangler%404.131.1) · [Pinned comparison](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/compare/570526276722ae57b250268a8af48fe0b1eaf774...00ae21fa83754462721a52bcd1ff9b4fbc12f898)

**Released findings:**

- `packages/config` is unchanged: object/function/promise composition and direct typed Worker references remain as in 4.130.0.
- Wrangler's experimental config loader, flags, development type generator, and build command are unchanged. Standalone `types` changes concern empty arrays (`unknown[]`) and generated container-image bindings; no new-config flag or alternate generation route was added. [Type command](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/00ae21fa83754462721a52bcd1ff9b4fbc12f898/packages/wrangler/src/type-generation/index.ts)
- Issue **#14396 remains open**, with its last recorded update June 23, 2026, verified using GitHub's authenticated API. [Issue](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/14396)
- Vite is **1.54.8**, and `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` is **1.1.8** at this release. Vitest 1.1.7 fixed test-helper declarations composing with Wrangler-generated runtime types under `skipLibCheck: false`; this does not provide standalone new-config type generation. [Vitest changelog](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/00ae21fa83754462721a52bcd1ff9b4fbc12f898/packages/vitest-plugin/CHANGELOG.md)
- No released change removes the prior Workflow-binding, preview-schema, top-level Container, or secret-value limitations.

**Unreleased, keep separate:**

Main **`8997652577fdbe97e39fb29bebd6777d3f82d3a3`** is four commits ahead. It adds `defineContainer`, sibling Container config exports, references from SQLite Durable Object exports, and Container build-output read/write support. The changeset explicitly says config support **has not been added to its consumers**—this is not evidence that Wrangler now supports a complete Container migration. [Config changeset](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/8997652577fdbe97e39fb29bebd6777d3f82d3a3/.changeset/curly-containers-config.md) · [Build-output changeset](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/8997652577fdbe97e39fb29bebd6777d3f82d3a3/.changeset/container-build-output.md)

5:Wrangler's “new config” is an experimental TypeScript configuration model: `cloudflare.config.ts` describes the Worker, while optional `wrangler.config.ts` describes Wrangler's tooling. It shipped behind `--x-new-config` in Wrangler 4.100.0. The latest verified release, **4.131.1**, retains the object composition and direct Worker references introduced in 4.130.0, but still does not connect the new generator to `wrangler types`. **Binding inference itself works without repeatedly running a generator**; this refresh verifies that distinction. [Introduction][intro] · [Release comparison][release-diff]
9:## Evidence boundary
13:- Previous refresh: Wrangler **4.130.0**, commit `570526276722ae57b250268a8af48fe0b1eaf774`, tested locally on September 9. [Release][release130]
14:- Latest verified npm release: Wrangler **4.131.1**, commit `00ae21fa83754462721a52bcd1ff9b4fbc12f898`, published September 11 at 14:22 UTC (September 12 in Sydney). Installed into a temporary directory and tested with Node **24.18.0**; the repository remains on 4.127.0. The shared `@cloudflare/config` implementation remains at **0.11.0** and is unchanged from 4.130.0. The command table below records fresh 4.131.1 observations. [Release][release1311] · [Pinned release comparison][release-diff]
17:## Changes since the September 9 refresh
19:- **Released config behavior is unchanged.** The new-config loader, dev type generator, and shared config package are unchanged between 4.130.0 and 4.131.1. The standalone type command did receive fixes for legacy empty-array variables and container-image binding types, but no new-config flag or loading/generation path. [Release comparison][release-diff] · [Type command][latest-types]
20:- **The reported command gap remains open.** Issue #14396 was still open when checked on September 12; local 4.131.1 experiments reproduce the failure independently of the issue report. [Issue][type-issue]
21:- **Related test tooling improved.** Current release-aligned versions are `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` 1.54.8 and `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.1.8. Vitest plugin 1.1.7 fixed test-helper declarations interacting with Wrangler-generated runtime types when `skipLibCheck` is false. That is separate from the missing standalone new-config generation path, and this repository still uses the older `vitest-pool-workers` package. [Vitest changelog][vitest-changelog] · [Release comparison][release-diff]
23:**Unreleased work, not 4.131.1 support:** upstream `main` at `8997652577fdbe97e39fb29bebd6777d3f82d3a3` adds `defineContainer`, sibling Container configuration exports, references from SQLite Durable Object exports, and build-output support for Container configs. Its changeset explicitly limits support to the config package and says it has not been added to consumers. This does not establish a working Container deployment path through Wrangler's new-config flag. [Config changeset][unreleased-containers] · [Build-output changeset][unreleased-container-output]
25:## What changes
43:## Minimal example and modes
45:This basic shape remains suitable for the investigated 4.127.0, 4.129.1, 4.130.0, and 4.131.1 APIs. The temporary fixture verified text/secret bindings and mode selection; this exact illustrative file is not a cyspbot deployment configuration.
81:There is no released `modes` override map in the inspected schema. A proposal for such a map was closed without merging; environment branching remains ordinary TypeScript. [Latest schema][latest-schema] · [Closed proposal][modes-proposal]
83:## New in 4.130.0: composition and Worker references
126:The local 4.131.1 build with `--env staging` emitted `name: "research-staging"` and `UPSTREAM: { type: "worker", worker: "upstream-staging" }`. Only `workers/default` was emitted. Local dev reported the referenced Worker as **not connected**: a config reference does not launch or deploy the referenced service.
128:## Command and tooling support
132:| `deploy --x-new-config --dry-run`                | Passed in 4.131.1 with composed settings, text/secret declarations, and a direct Worker config reference. No `.d.ts` output.                                                                                                                                                           |

The new-config type-generation file is used by development, not this standalone command. Still fails in 4.131.1; no new-config command integration was added.                                                           |
137:| `types` with only `cloudflare.config.ts` present | Failed in 4.131.1: `No config file detected. This command requires a Wrangler configuration file.`                                                                                                                                                                                     |
143:The 4.131.1 command experiments are local observations, supported by the [build implementation][build], [loader][loader], [development type generator][dev-types], [standalone type command][latest-types], [initial release scope][intro], and first-party [Vite test][vite-new-config] / [new Vitest plugin fixture][vitest]. Running a command with `--help` is insufficient to test whether a hidden flag is accepted during execution.
145:### Why dev works while the standalone command does not
149:### Binding inference without regeneration
160:**Verified on 4.131.1:** a focused TypeScript 7.0.2 fixture checked a literal text binding, a string secret, and rejection of missing bindings/wrong values. After adding another text binding to the config, a second compiler run recognized it and rejected a wrong literal without changing `env.ts`, the generated declaration file, or the runtime declarations; their SHA-256 hashes were unchanged. The compiler check used `strict: true` and `skipLibCheck: true`, so it verifies application binding inference, not full third-party declaration compatibility. [Inference implementation][inference] · [Generated bridge][generator]
166:## Migration limitations and ownership
168:**API volatility is observable between released versions.** At 4.127.0, Worker/DO/dispatch/tail targets use `workerName`; by 4.129.1 they use `worker`. At 4.130.0, the definition wrapper and instance binding methods were removed in favor of ordinary configs and direct references. The shared config changelog also records the recent move of development binding options under `dev`. Pin the entire related toolchain when experimenting. [Config changes][config-changes]
170:**Binding parity is incomplete.** In the released 4.131.1 schema, Workflow bindings remain excluded/commented out, Worker previews remain a TODO, and there is no top-level containers configuration. These are specific schema gaps, not evidence that all other legacy properties are supported. Inventory the fields actually needed before converting a real deployment. [Released schema][latest-schema]
174:**Executable configuration is not a resource ownership system.** Helpers such as `bindings.kv({ id })` map into existing Wrangler binding fields; omitting an ID can enter Wrangler's existing automatic provisioning behavior. Automatic provisioning is also available in ordinary JSONC and is documented as beta. A typed helper is not evidence of a Terraform-style plan, import, destroy, or whole-account reconciliation contract. Remote resource reuse, configuration writeback, and repeated deployment behavior for this TypeScript path were not tested here. Use explicit production identities supplied by the deployment owner until those behaviors are verified for the exact resource and tool versions. [Conversion][convert] · [Automatic provisioning][docs]
176:**Composition advice changed in 4.130.0.** The previous warning against spreading `defineWorker` results applied to the inspected 4.127.0/4.129.1 symbol-wrapper implementation. It is superseded for object-form configs by the ordinary values described above. Existing code that calls definition-instance binding helpers must migrate to `bindings.worker` / `bindings.durableObject`. Updated the [research note](/Users/cysp/src/cyspbot/docs/research/wrangler-new-config.md) against **Wrangler 4.131.1**, current as of September 12. [Release](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/releases/tag/wrangler%404.131.1)

- **The CLI gap remains:** `types --x-new-config` still fails; plain `types` does not discover the TypeScript config. Dev generates both binding and runtime declarations.
- **Binding inference works without regeneration:** I verified that adding a binding updates the inferred `Env` type without changing any declaration files. Runtime declarations still need separate maintenance.
- **Composition is unchanged** from 4.130.0: object spread and direct Worker references work.
- **Unreleased Containers support exists on `main`**, but its changeset explicitly says consumers have not integrated it yet. It is not working Wrangler support. [Changeset](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/8997652577fdbe97e39fb29bebd6777d3f82d3a3/.changeset/curly-containers-config.md)

The note now treats missing CLI integration separately from binding-type capability. Repository dependencies remain unchanged.
